old_caption: The video captures a close-up view of a pottery wheel, focusing on the hands of an individual shaping a clay pot. The person's hands, covered in clay, are seen using a trimming tool to shape the rim of the pot, which is rotating at a consistent, moderate speed on the wheel. The pot has a cylindrical form with distinct horizontal ridges. The background remains blurred, keeping the viewer's focus entirely on the hands and the evolving clay piece. The overall atmosphere conveys a sense of craftsmanship and dedication to the art of pottery. The potter also uses a sponge to smooth the clay while the wheel is rotating.
original_wisa_caption: The video captures a close-up view of a pottery wheel in action, focusing on the hands of an individual skillfully shaping a clay pot. The person's hands, covered in clay, are seen carefully molding the top part of the pot, which is spinning rapidly on the wheel. The pot has a cylindrical base and a narrower neck, indicating the early stages of its creation. As the scene progresses, the individual uses a green sponge to smooth out the surface of the clay, ensuring it is even and free of imperfections. The sponge moves methodically around the pot, highlighting the meticulous attention to detail required in pottery making. The background remains blurred, keeping the viewer's focus entirely on the hands and the evolving clay piece. The overall atmosphere conveys a sense of craftsmanship and dedication to the art of pottery.
caption: The video captures a close-up of a reddish-brown clay vessel on a spinning pottery wheel, its foot, shoulder and open mouth turning with rotational blur. A pink caliper-style tool rests against the vessel's upper-right shoulder, its handle extending off the right edge. In the blurred background, a seated potter in a gray shirt and green pants keeps wet hands hovering above the clay without clear contact. Then an arm and hand sweep across the front of the vessel from the left, occluding the spinning clay before withdrawing toward the lower right. After this pass, a hand holding a green sponge enters from the left and presses it against the vessel's base on the wheel head. The sponge wipes that lower area as the wheel turns, the hand remaining there while the wheel keeps turning. Throughout, the caliper's contact point and the vessel's silhouette stay essentially unchanged as the process continues.
